relativistic corrections to galaxy clustering can indeed provide a powerful tool to distinguish between dark energy and modified gravity, but only in the case where the dark energy equation of state is known.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the relativistic corrections in the linear perturbation theory of gravity and dark energy can be calibrated in a model-independent fashion and that these corrections are significant for the normal branch of DGP gravity and for dark energy models with large values of the equation-of-state parameter.
, in the parametrized post-friedmann formalism, the relativistic effects are not negligible in general, and the galaxy-density field is a good tool to test gravity and dark energy.

, in general, the relativistic correction to the matter density field contains additional information on dark energy and gravity that needs to be taken in consistent horizon-scale testing departures from Λ CDM using galaxy-density fields.
